name: Gemeinsames Registerportal der Länder
description: Gemeinsames Registerportal der Länder is the official electronic system through which the German commercial, cooperative, partnership, company and association registers are searched and their filed documents inspected. The registers themselves are kept by the competent local courts; the portal is the retrieval route the Länder justice administrations designated for them, and it also carries the register announcements.

operator.name: Landesjustizverwaltungen (justice administrations of the German Länder)

bestFor: Searching any German register entry from a single national entry point rather than court by court.
Inspecting the documents an entity has filed with its commercial register.
notRecommendedFor: Treating a retrieval as the register itself, since the registers are kept by the courts and the portal provides access to them.
Relying on structured retrieval where the official printout is what is needed, because the operator describes the structured service as non-binding.
pros: One portal reaches the registers of every Bundesland, which are otherwise kept court by court.
It covers the commercial, cooperative, partnership, company and association registers, and the register announcements alongside them.
Documents filed with the register can be inspected through it, not only the register entries themselves.
A court can certify that data retrieved through the portal matches the register content, so an official copy is obtainable by this route.
cons: The portal is the designated retrieval system, not the register itself. Under the Commercial Code the commercial register is kept electronically by the courts, and the portal is the electronic information and communication system the Länder justice administrations determined for access to it.
The operator describes structured retrieval as a non-binding service whose content may differ from the current official printout.
Because each register is kept by a local court, a question about the legal status of an entry belongs to that court rather than to the portal.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04; source-of-record corrected 2026-08-05 (Wave 1D). CORRECTION: this record previously carried primaryRegistryType company-register and described the portal as "aggregating" the registers, which asserted that the portal constitutes the German commercial register. It does not. Handelsgesetzbuch § 8(1) provides that the commercial register is kept electronically by the courts, and Handelsregisterverordnung § 1 assigns each register to the Amtsgericht at a Landgericht seat. Handelsgesetzbuch § 9(1) provides that the Länder justice administrations determine the electronic information and communication system through which register data may be retrieved, and that the Länder may determine a joint, central cross-Land system. The portal is therefore the designated access and publication route, not the constitutive register. Reclassified to public-filing-database because § 9(1) covers inspection of the register AND of the documents filed with it; the earlier note claiming the evidence established "register aggregation, not a filed-document database" was wrong on that point. Operator corrected to the Landesjustizverwaltungen, which is the body § 9(1) charges with determining and running the retrieval system; the courts are named in prose as the holders of the registers rather than as the portal operator. Score unchanged: the correction concerns what the system is, not how reliable or useful it is, and court certification under § 9(3) still runs through this route.

name: Bundesanzeiger
description: German federal gazette publishing statutory corporate announcements and filed annual financial statements.

operator.name: Bundesanzeiger Verlag, on behalf of the Federal Ministry of Justice

bestFor: Reading a German company’s filed financial statements
Tracking statutory corporate announcements
notRecommendedFor: Company discovery
Marketing exposure
recommendedIndustries: Any German company with disclosure obligations
pros: Central platform for legally mandated German disclosures
cons: Publication is an obligation rather than an opt-in listing
Filing costs were not established
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. Issued by the Federal Ministry of Justice, operated by Bundesanzeiger Verlag.

name: Unternehmensregister
description: Unternehmensregister is the German central platform on which company data that must be published is brought together and made electronically retrievable. It carries register information transmitted from the commercial, cooperative, partnership and company registers, together with accounts and capital-market disclosures, and is constituted for that purpose by the Commercial Code.

publicAccess.notes: The platform is reached without an account. Whether every retrieval is free of charge was not established, so the fee position is left unknown rather than assumed.

bestFor: Reaching German company register information, published accounts and capital-market disclosures from one central platform.
Finding what a German company has actually published, rather than only that it exists.
notRecommendedFor: Use as the constitutive commercial register, which is kept by the courts and reached through the register portal.
Assuming everything shown is free, because the fee position for retrievals was not established.
recommendedIndustries: German companies subject to publication duties
pros: It is constituted in the Commercial Code as the central platform for company data that must be published, so its role is statutory rather than editorial.
Register information, published accounts and capital-market disclosures are brought together in one place instead of three.
Data reaches it by transmission from the source registers, so it is a government channel rather than a commercial re-publication.
cons: It is a central publication platform, not the constitutive register. The German commercial registers are kept by the courts, and the register portal is the designated route to them.
Whether every retrieval is free of charge was not established, so cost should be checked before relying on it for bulk work.
What appears depends on what an entity was obliged to publish, so absence of a document is not evidence that an obligation was breached.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the platform’s own pages and from the Commercial Code. The site publishes itself as "Die zentrale Plattform zu Unternehmensdaten" and states that data subject to publication duties is centrally brought together and made electronically retrievable. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Handelsgesetzbuch § 8b constitutes the Unternehmensregister in federal statute. It is a publication platform: the underlying commercial, cooperative, partnership and company registers remain constituted by the courts under HGB § 8(1). RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundesministerium der Justiz, to which HGB § 8b assigns the keeping of the register. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Bundesanzeiger Verlag GmbH operates the platform. It is the technical operator and is deliberately NOT recorded as the operator field, which names the responsible authority. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at unternehmensregister.de. This record is deliberately separate from de-registerportal: the register portal is the designated retrieval route to the court-held registers, while the Unternehmensregister is the statutory central publication platform. Neither is the constitutive register.

name: Transparenzregister
description: Transparenzregister is the German register of beneficial owners, established by the Money Laundering Act. Entities subject to the Act report the natural persons who ultimately own or control them, and the register records those persons rather than the entities themselves.

publicAccess.notes: Inspection requires registration on the portal and is fee-bearing. The application is client-rendered and the inspection flow itself was not exercised, so the precise identity checks applied are not asserted.

bestFor: Establishing who ultimately owns or controls a German entity, where the ownership chain is not visible in the commercial register.
Anti-money-laundering due diligence that requires the beneficial owner rather than the registered shareholder.
notRecommendedFor: A quick free lookup, because inspection requires registration and carries a fee.
Confirming that a company exists, which is the commercial register kept by the courts.
recommendedIndustries: German entities subject to beneficial-ownership reporting
pros: It records the natural persons behind an entity, which no other German register sets out to do.
Keeping the register is a sovereign federal task under the Money Laundering Act, so its basis is statutory rather than contractual.
It covers entities across legal forms rather than companies alone.
cons: Inspection is not free and requires registration on the portal, so it is not comparable to the open company registers.
It records reported beneficial owners. A report is made by the entity, so the register reflects what was declared rather than what was independently established.
It does not establish that an entity exists or who legally represents it. That is the commercial register kept by the courts, reached through the register portal.
The application is client-rendered and the inspection flow was not exercised, so the exact identity checks applied to a searcher are not stated here.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from official German sources, including the Money Laundering Act provisions constituting the register. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Geldwäschegesetz §§ 18 to 26 constitute the register; § 18 establishes it and declares its keeping a sovereign federal task. Since 2021 it is a full register rather than a catch-all reference register. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundesministerium der Finanzen, which under the Act may transfer the keeping of the register to a private body by way of Beleihung. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Bundesanzeiger Verlag GmbH keeps the register as the beleihene registerführende Stelle under the implementing ordinance. It is the entrusted operator and is deliberately not recorded as the responsible authority. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The portal at transparenzregister.de, where inspection requires registration and is fee-bearing. Access booleans reflect what was established: registration is required and inspection is fee-bearing, so loginRequired is true and freeToSearch is false; the precise identity-verification step was not exercised and stays null. No search URL is published because no anonymous search surface exists to link to.

name: DPMAregister
description: DPMAregister is the official register and publication database of the German Patent and Trade Mark Office. It carries the office’s registers for patents, utility models, topographies and supplementary protection certificates, for trade marks and geographical indications, and for designs, each with its own search interface.

publicAccess.notes: The overview page and the basic search interfaces for patents, trade marks and designs were all retrieved anonymously without any credential. Rate limiting was not probed and no CAPTCHA was encountered, but absence was not established, so no CAPTCHA claim is made either way.

bestFor: Checking the status, owner and filing history of a German patent, utility model, trade mark or registered design.
Establishing whether a mark or design is already registered in Germany before filing.
notRecommendedFor: Company verification. This register records industrial property rights, not the existence or officers of a business.
Relying on the English interface for a legally binding statement, because the office treats only the German register excerpt as binding.
recommendedIndustries: Holders and applicants of German industrial property rights
pros: It is the German office’s own register database, so it is the authoritative source for the status of a German industrial property right rather than a commercial copy of it.
Three separate rights families each have their own dedicated search entry point, which keeps patents, trade marks and designs from being conflated in one undifferentiated result set.
Searching is free and worked anonymously, with no account required to reach any of the basic search interfaces.
cons: Only the German-language register excerpt is legally binding. The office labels its English output a non-binding translation.
It is a register of rights. It does not record whether a right is being used, whether it is commercially significant, or whether it is being disputed outside the register.
The office’s main site refused automated requests behind a JavaScript interstitial, so background documentation had to be read from the register host itself.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the register database’s own pages at register.dpma.de. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The registers themselves are constituted by the German industrial property statutes — the Patentgesetz, the Gebrauchsmustergesetz, the Markengesetz and the Designgesetz — and are kept by the Deutsches Patent- und Markenamt, which grants and records the rights. This database is the office’s own register, not a third-party view of it. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Deutsches Patent- und Markenamt. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: None found. No supplier is named on any page fetched; the application is served from the office’s own register host. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The database at register.dpma.de, whose overview page offers three labelled basic-search entry points: patents, utility models, topographies and supplementary protection certificates; trade marks and geographical indications; and designs. Registry types: patent-register, trademark-register and registered-design-register are recorded separately because the vocabulary treats them as separate rights with separate registers even where one office runs all three, and the designs entry point was confirmed on the office’s own overview page. public-filing-database was considered and rejected: file inspection was not exercised, so no filed-document function is asserted. The official name uses a plain hyphen, as the register’s own heading does; an en dash appeared in an earlier draft and was corrected. The German industrial property office must not be confused with the German commercial register systems already published, none of which shares a host with this one.

name: Insolvenzbekanntmachungen
description: Insolvenzbekanntmachungen is the German portal on which the insolvency courts make the announcements required by the Insolvency Code. Publication there is the statutory public announcement of a proceeding; the proceeding itself is conducted and recorded by the court.

operator.name: Ministerium der Justiz des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen

publicAccess.notes: The portal was reached anonymously with no credential and no fee. Requests to www.insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de redirect to neu.insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de, which is where the pages are actually served. No CAPTCHA was encountered, but absence was not established and none is asserted. The portal states that results are capped at 1,000 hits, that names must match exactly, and that result pages cannot be linked to directly.

bestFor: Reading the official announcement of a German insolvency proceeding, including the opening decision and the appointed administrator.
Checking whether a named German debtor has had an insolvency proceeding announced, when the exact registered name is known.
notRecommendedFor: Screening by approximate or partial name. The portal returns a hit only on an exact match with the entry as the court wrote it.
Treating the portal as the register of the proceeding. It is the statutory publication medium; the proceeding is recorded by the insolvency court.
pros: It is the single national medium in which every German insolvency court makes its statutory announcements, so one search covers all Länder rather than sixteen gazettes.
Searching is free and anonymous, with no account, no fee and no identity step reached at any point.

The portal documents its own limits explicitly — the hit cap, the exact-match rule and the staggered dates from which each Land’s announcements are carried — instead of leaving a user to discover them.
cons: Names must match exactly, including suffixes such as “AG” or “GmbH & Co. KG” as recorded in the commercial register, so a near-miss returns nothing rather than a suggestion.
Every search is capped at 1,000 hits, which matters for any attempt to check a large group of counterparties at once.
Result pages cannot be linked to, and a result session lasts sixty minutes, so a finding cannot be cited by URL and has to be re-run.
It carries the announcements the Insolvency Code requires. It does not hold the court file, the creditor filings or the outcome of the proceeding.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the portal’s own pages, including its imprint and its search guidance. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The proceedings are conducted and recorded by the German insolvency courts; this portal is where those courts make the announcements the Insolvency Code requires. Its imprint states that selection and publication of the information rest on § 9 InsO together with § 2 of the ordinance on public announcements in insolvency proceedings on the internet of 12 February 2002, as amended in 2019. The portal is therefore the statutory publication medium and is not itself the register of a proceeding. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Ministerium der Justiz des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen, named as the publisher in the imprint, operating the service within the joint justice portal of the federation and the Länder. The imprint names no individual as responsible under media law. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: None found. No supplier is named on any page fetched, and no technical operator is asserted here. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The portal reached at www.insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de, which redirects to neu.insolvenzbekanntmachungen.de where the search and guidance pages are served. Registry type: insolvency-register, because the system publishes insolvency proceedings as a distinct dataset, which is what the type requires. The record deliberately does not describe the portal as the register in which a proceeding is constituted — that is the court — and the description, the second entry under what it is not recommended for, and this note all state the distinction. The portal itself carries a warning that private registers and invoices are circulated in imitation of official justice publications; that warning is why the distinction between the official medium and a commercial copy is worth stating.

name: BaFin Unternehmensdatenbank
description: The BaFin company database is the German financial supervisor’s searchable record of the undertakings it supervises. It covers credit institutions, leasing and factoring institutions, financial services institutions, capital management companies and further supervised categories, and carries the date its data was last updated.

publicAccess.notes: The search form was served directly and anonymously, including its category filters and a stated data-currency date, but no query was executed, so no result behaviour, fee or rate limit is asserted and no search URL is published. Access booleans stay null because loading a form is not the same as observing a search.

bestFor: Checking whether a German financial undertaking is supervised, and in which supervised category it falls.
Reaching the supervisor’s own record of an institution rather than an aggregated European compilation.
notRecommendedFor: Finding warnings about unauthorised firms, which the supervisor publishes separately from this database.
Treating supervision as endorsement. The database records that an undertaking is supervised, not that it is sound or well run.
pros: It is the supervisor’s own database, so it is the national source rather than a European compilation of national notifications.
It distinguishes supervised categories explicitly, so a credit institution is not conflated with a financial services institution or a capital management company.
The page states the date to which its data is current, which makes the freshness of an answer checkable rather than assumed.
cons: It records supervision status only. It is not a statement about an institution’s solvency, conduct or the suitability of its products.
Warning lists and unauthorised-business notices are published elsewhere by the same supervisor, so this database is not where a reader learns that a firm is not permitted.
No query was executed during verification, so result formatting, export options and any rate limit are unestablished and are not asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the database itself, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The served form carried a stated data-currency date and the category filters for supervised institution types. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The supervisory and authorisation decisions of the German financial supervisor, taken under German financial supervision law. For credit institutions within the European banking union the authorisation decision may sit with the European supervisor while the national supervisor conducts the procedure, so the record does not claim the database constitutes the authorisation. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The database is served from the supervisor’s own portal host; no external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The company database on the supervisor’s portal. Scoping decision: the supervisor publishes several databases and lists. Only the company database is published here, because it is the one coherent searchable register of supervised undertakings. Warning lists and unauthorised-business notices were deliberately excluded — they record the opposite of authorisation and would need their own classification decision rather than being folded in. Registry type: financial-services-register.

name: Bundesweites Amtliches Anwaltsverzeichnis
description: The official nationwide directory of lawyers admitted in Germany, operated by the Bundesrechtsanwaltskammer over the registers of the regional bars. It answers one question — whether a person is admitted to practise as a Rechtsanwalt in Germany — and admission is required to practise, not merely to use the title.

publicAccess.notes: The search form was served anonymously with no credential, in German and English, with fields for name, professional title, specialist subtitle, firm, address and bar, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content, coverage and any rate limit were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a named person is admitted to practise as a lawyer anywhere in Germany.
Confirming that a European or non-German lawyer is established in Germany under the Federal Lawyers Act.
notRecommendedFor: Judging whether a lawyer is suitable for a matter. The chamber states it may not assess or recommend individual lawyers.
Treating a nil result as proof that someone never practised. Admission can end, and the directory shows current status.
pros: It is the official nationwide directory and covers every lawyer admitted in Germany, so one search replaces twenty-eight regional ones.
It reaches beyond German lawyers to European lawyers and to lawyers from other states established in Germany under section 206 of the Federal Lawyers Act.
It is served in both German and English, which is unusual for a national professional register.
cons: Admission is required to practise, not only to use the title, so an entry means more here than in a protected-title register — but it still says nothing about competence in any field.
The federal chamber operates the directory; it is not the body that admitted anyone. Admission and discipline sit with the regional bar, which the search page states directly.
It records individual lawyers and their firms, not a firm’s quality, and specialist subtitles are conferred by the local bar rather than centrally.
The chamber states it is not entitled to give legal advice, to examine the conduct of individual lawyers, to recommend them, or to check fee invoices, so inclusion establishes none of those things.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the search host and of the chamber’s own describing page, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The search host titles itself "Official Nationwide Register Of Lawyers" and states it covers "all Rechtsanwälte/Rechtsanwältinnen and European lawyers admitted in Germany as well as lawyers from other countries which are established in Germany under 206 of the Federal Lawyers Act and all legal advisers (“Rechtsbeistände”) who are members of a Bar". The chamber’s page states the directory "umfasst alle in Deutschland zugelassenen Rechtsanwältinnen und Rechtsanwälte". FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The admission decisions of the twenty-eight regional Rechtsanwaltskammern under the Bundesrechtsanwaltsordnung. The search host states that "Disciplinary control is exercised by the respective regional Bar to which the lawyer is admitted", so the federal directory is an interface over regional registers and is not itself the source of record. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundesrechtsanwaltskammer, a public-law corporation and the umbrella body of the regional bars. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: bea-brak.de, the chamber’s own electronic-communication platform, which also serves the beA system. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at bravsearch.bea-brak.de. URL note: the chamber’s own link (www.bea-brak.de/bravsearch/search.brak) and the widely cited rechtsanwaltsregister.org both redirect cross-host to bravsearch.bea-brak.de/bravsearch/, which is recorded here as the canonical entry.  Duplicate decision: BRAK’s separate "Anwaltssuche" page is NOT a second record. It is a signpost that points readers to the regional chambers’ own search services and to this directory; it is not a system of its own.

name: WPK Berufsregister
description: The professional register of German public auditors and audit firms, kept by the Wirtschaftsprüferkammer under section 37 of the Public Accountant Act. The same register also discharges the statutory auditor register required by the EU Audit Directive, so one system serves both purposes.

publicAccess.notes: The register is described by the chamber as publicly accessible with current data. The search application was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. It renders its interface with JavaScript and no query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking that a named auditor or audit firm is entitled to carry out statutory audits in Germany.
Confirming the status of an EU, EEA or third-country audit firm registered in Germany.
notRecommendedFor: Judging audit quality. Registration records entitlement, not how any engagement was performed.
Assuming a person absent from it cannot do any accountancy work. Only statutory audit is reserved to the professions recorded here.
pros: Its statutory basis is stated on the chamber’s own page: section 37(1) sentence 1 of the Wirtschaftsprüferordnung.
One register discharges two legal functions, so there is no second national auditor list to reconcile it against.
It covers firms as well as individuals, including EU and EEA audit firms and third-country auditors and firms.
cons: Registration is required to carry out statutory audits, so it is a licence to practise a reserved activity rather than a protected title — but it is not a statement about the quality of any audit.

It mixes populations with different entitlements — public auditors, sworn accountants, audit firms, foreign firms and cooperative audit associations — so a hit alone does not tell a reader what the entry permits.
The register is kept by the chamber; entries follow the chamber’s own admission and recognition decisions, which is not the same as supervision of an individual audit.
The search application renders with JavaScript, so it could not be exercised and nothing about result content or coverage is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the chamber’s register page and search entry, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The chamber states: "Die WPK führt ein Berufsregister für Wirtschaftsprüfer und Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaften (§ 37 Abs. 1 Satz 1 WPO)" and that "Neben der Erfassung der Daten der Mitglieder der WPK erfüllt das Berufsregister zugleich die Aufgabe des Abschlussprüferregisters im Sinne der Abschlussprüferrichtlinie (Richtlinie 2006/43/EG)". Listed populations: Wirtschaftsprüfer/vereidigte Buchprüfer; Wirtschaftsprüfungs-/Buchprüfungsgesellschaften; EU- und EWR-Abschlussprüfungsgesellschaften; Drittstaatsprüfer und Drittstaatsprüfungsgesellschaften; genossenschaftliche Prüfungsverbände und Prüfungsstellen der Sparkassen- und Giroverbände. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The professional register kept by the Wirtschaftsprüferkammer under section 37(1) sentence 1 WPO, which simultaneously constitutes the statutory auditor register under Directive 2006/43/EC. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Wirtschaftsprüferkammer, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The application is served from the chamber’s own domain and no external supplier is named. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The chamber’s public register search at wpk.de/berufsregister/. Duplicate decisions, both rejections. The chamber’s "Liste der Abschlussprüfer und Prüfungsgesellschaften" is a DOWNLOAD published for selection procedures under Article 16(3) of EU Regulation 537/2014 — a publication derived from this register, not a register. Its "Suche nach Spezialkenntnissen" is a filtered view of the same register, not a separate system. Recorded so neither is proposed again. Also noted and not researched: the Abschlussprüferaufsichtsstelle (APAS) publishes a separate list of firms meeting a 15 per cent fee-share threshold; that is a different body.

name: Bundesweites Amtliches Patentanwaltsverzeichnis
description: The official nationwide directory of patent attorneys admitted in Germany, kept by the Patentanwaltskammer. It covers individual patent attorneys, in-house patent attorneys and professional practice companies, and admission is required to practise rather than only to use the title.
englishName: Official Nationwide Register of Patent Attorneys

publicAccess.notes: The search mask was served anonymously with no credential, with fields for salutation, title, name, place and company, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking that a named patent attorney is admitted in Germany before instructing them.
Confirming that a patent practice company is admitted under the Patent Attorney Regulations.
notRecommendedFor: Choosing an attorney by technical field. The directory records admission, not expertise in a technology.
Assuming coverage of European Patent Attorneys generally. Only those established in Germany under the applicable provisions appear.
pros: The chamber describes it as an electronic directory of all patent attorneys admitted in Germany, maintained on a daily basis.
It covers professional practice companies under sections 52f and 159 of the Patent Attorney Regulations, so firms are searchable and not only individuals.
It reaches European patent attorneys established in Germany and patent attorneys from other states, each shown with the professional title of their home state.
cons: Admission is required to practise as a patent attorney, so this is a licence register — but an entry is not a statement about experience in any technical field or trade.
It records individuals and practice companies together, so a result must be read carefully to know which kind of entry has been returned.
The chamber keeps the directory and admits its members; it does not supervise the conduct of any individual mandate.
The application issues a session-specific address on entry, so a copied link is not a durable citation and a reader should return through the register’s own domain.
Absence does not establish that a person never practised. Admission can end, and the directory shows who is admitted now rather than a history of the profession.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the chamber’s own site to the register, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The chamber states patent attorneys in Germany "sind in einer Körperschaft des öffentlichen Rechts organisiert, die sich selbst verwaltet", and that it "hat ein elektronisches Verzeichnis aller in Deutschland zugelassenen Patentanwältinnen und Patentanwälte eingerichtet … Das Verzeichnis wird tagesaktuell geführt". The register page titles itself "Bundesweites Amtliches Patentanwaltsverzeichnis" and states it also covers "zugelassenen Berufsausübungsgesellschaften gemäß § 52f PAO und ausländischen Berufsausübungsgesellschaften gemäß § 159 PAO", plus European patent attorneys under § 20 EuPAG and patent attorneys from other states under § 157 Abs. 1 PAO. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Admission to the profession under the Patentanwaltsordnung. The chamber admits and records; the directory reflects that decision. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Patentanwaltskammer, a self-governing public-law corporation. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: An ASP.NET application on the chamber’s patentanwaltsregister.de domain, which mints a session-specific path on entry. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at patentanwaltsregister.de. Access note: entry to the bare domain returned HTTP 200 and redirected to a session URL of the form /(X(1)S(…))/default.aspx. The stable entry recorded here is the bare domain.

name: Amtliches Steuerberaterverzeichnis
description: The official nationwide register of German tax advisers, tax agents and tax advisory practice companies, kept by the Bundessteuerberaterkammer under section 86b of the Tax Advisory Act. It records who is entitled to give unrestricted assistance in tax matters in Germany.

publicAccess.notes: The chamber states the register is accessible to anyone. The search was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking that a named person or company may give unrestricted assistance in tax matters in Germany.
Confirming that a tax advisory practice company is recognised or entered in the professional register.
notRecommendedFor: Finding an adviser for a particular specialism. The chamber states the register does not serve that purpose.
Concluding from absence that a person may not act at all in tax matters. Two separate registers cover foreign and partially authorised providers.
pros: Its statutory basis is stated on the register itself: section 86b of the Steuerberatungsgesetz, as an electronic overall register.
It covers appointed tax advisers and tax agents together with recognised practice companies, so firms are searchable as well as individuals.
The chamber states plainly that the register is accessible to anyone, and it can be narrowed to a place or postcode area.
cons: Appointment is required to give unrestricted assistance in tax matters, so this is a licence register — but the chamber states the register is not a way to search for an adviser with a particular specialism or qualification.

The federal chamber publishes the register, but the underlying professional registers are kept by the locally competent regional chambers, which the register states in reference to section 86b(1) sentence 3.

Absence from this register does not mean a person may not act in tax matters at all. Foreign providers acting temporarily and persons with partial authorisation are recorded in two separate registers kept by the same chamber.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the federal chamber’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The register states: "Die Bundessteuerberaterkammer führt nach § 86b Steuerberatungsgesetz ein elektronisches Gesamtverzeichnis aller in Deutschland bestellten Steuerberater und Steuerbevollmächtigten sowie aller im Berufsregister eingetragenen steuerberatenden Berufsausübungsgesellschaften. Das amtliche Steuerberaterverzeichnis ist jedermann zugänglich." It also states it "dient dagegen nicht dazu, nach einem Steuerberater für ein bestimmtes Fachgebiet oder mit speziellen Qualifikationen zu suchen", and that it "basiert auf den Daten der Berufsregister, die von den örtlich zuständigen Steuerberaterkammern geführt werden (vgl. § 86b Abs. 1 Satz 3 StBerG)". FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The professional registers kept by the locally competent Steuerberaterkammern; the federal register aggregates them under § 86b StBerG. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundessteuerberaterkammer, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: A berufs-org.de subdomain of its own. The chamber’s two other statutory registers run on separate subdomains of the same parent domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at steuerberaterverzeichnis.berufs-org.de. Separation decision: kept distinct from the § 3b and § 3g registers. Three different statutory bases, three different authorisation regimes, three different populations AND three different hosts; merging them because the chamber runs all three would misstate what any entry permits. No shared-host group is declared, because the three registers do not share a host — each has its own subdomain.

name: Verzeichnis der zur vorübergehenden Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen befugten Personen
description: The statutory register of service providers from other EU or EEA states or Switzerland who are authorised to give temporary and occasional assistance in tax matters in Germany, kept by the Bundessteuerberaterkammer under section 3b of the Tax Advisory Act.
officialName: Verzeichnis der zur vorübergehenden und gelegentlichen Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen befugten Personen
nativeName: Verzeichnis der zur vorübergehenden und gelegentlichen Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen befugten Personen
englishName: Register of Persons Authorised for Temporary and Occasional Assistance in Tax Matters

publicAccess.notes: The chamber states the register is accessible to anyone. The search was served anonymously with no credential, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a foreign provider is registered to give temporary and occasional assistance in tax matters in Germany.
Distinguishing a cross-border provider from a tax adviser appointed in Germany.
notRecommendedFor: Assessing a foreign provider’s qualifications or specialisms. The register states it does not serve that purpose.
Treating an entry as equivalent to appointment as a German tax adviser. The authorisation is temporary and occasional.
pros: Its statutory basis is stated on the register itself: section 3b of the Steuerberatungsgesetz, covering providers authorised under section 3a.
It makes a population visible that would otherwise be invisible in the main tax adviser register.
The chamber states the register is accessible to anyone and can be narrowed to a place or postcode area.
cons: The authorisation recorded here is for temporary and occasional assistance only. It is not an appointment as a German tax adviser and must not be read as one.

Only foreign providers temporarily entered in the professional register of the competent regional chamber following a notification under section 3a(2) are listed, so it is not a general directory of foreign advisers.
The register states it does not serve to establish what qualifications or specialisations a foreign provider has.
Absence here does not mean a person may not act in Germany. They may be appointed as a tax adviser, or hold partial authorisation recorded in a separate register.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the federal chamber’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The register states: "Die Bundessteuerberaterkammer führt nach § 3b Steuerberatungsgesetz (StBerG) ein elektronisches Verzeichnis über die Dienstleister aus anderen Mitgliedstaaten der Europäischen Union, den Vertragsstaaten des Abkommens über den Europäischen Wirtschaftraum oder der Schweiz, die nach § 3a StBerG in Deutschland zur vorübergehenden und gelegentlichen Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen befugt sind", that only those "aufgrund einer Meldung nach § 3a Abs. 2 StBerG im Berufsregister der zuständigen Steuerberaterkammer vorübergehend eingetragen sind (§ 3a Abs. 3 StBerG)" appear, and that "Das Verzeichnis ist jedermann zugänglich." FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Temporary entry in the professional register of the competent regional Steuerberaterkammer following a notification under § 3a(2) StBerG; the federal register publishes it under § 3b StBerG. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundessteuerberaterkammer, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: A berufs-org.de subdomain of its own, separate from the chamber’s two other statutory registers. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at eu-dienstleister-in-steuersachen.berufs-org.de. Separation decision: distinct statutory basis (§ 3b), distinct population and its own host, separate from the § 86b main register and the § 3g partial-access register. Not a filter of either.

name: Verzeichnis der partiell zugelassenen Personen nach § 3d StBerG
description: The statutory register of persons holding partial authorisation to give restricted commercial assistance in tax matters in Germany on the basis of a professional qualification obtained in the EU, EEA or Switzerland, kept by the Bundessteuerberaterkammer under section 3g of the Tax Advisory Act.
officialName: Verzeichnis der partiell zugelassenen Personen nach § 3d Steuerberatungsgesetz
nativeName: Verzeichnis der partiell zugelassenen Personen nach § 3d Steuerberatungsgesetz
englishName: Register of Persons with Partial Authorisation in Tax Matters

publicAccess.notes: The chamber states the register is accessible to anyone. The search form was served anonymously with no credential, with fields for surname or company, place and postcode, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a person holds partial authorisation to assist in tax matters in Germany.
Establishing that an entry carries a restricted rather than a full entitlement.
notRecommendedFor: Treating an entry as unrestricted authorisation. The entitlement covers only the activities for which partial access was granted.
Concluding from absence that a person cannot act. They may be a fully appointed tax adviser or a temporary cross-border provider.
pros: Its statutory basis is stated on the register itself: section 3g of the Steuerberatungsgesetz, for permissions granted under section 3d(1).
It makes an easily misread population explicit rather than folding it into the main register.
The chamber states the register is accessible to anyone and can be narrowed to a place or postcode area.
cons: The entitlement is partial. The register states that it covers only the activities for which partial access was granted, and is further limited to the scope of the entitlement in the home state.
Only persons entered in the professional register of the competent regional chamber appear, so the federal register depends on a regional entry.
An entry is not an appointment as a German tax adviser and does not permit unrestricted assistance in tax matters.
Absence here does not establish that a person may not act, because full appointment and temporary cross-border authorisation are recorded elsewhere.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the federal chamber’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The register states: "Die Bundessteuerberaterkammer führt nach § 3g Steuerberatungsgesetz (StBerG) ein elektronisches Verzeichnis aller Personen mit einer in einem Mitgliedstaat der Europäischen Union, einem Vertragsstaat über das Abkommen über den Europäischen Wirtschaftsraum oder in der Schweiz erworbenen Berufsqualifikation, denen nach § 3d Abs. 1 StBerG eine Erlaubnis zu beschränkter geschäftsmäßiger Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen (partieller Zugang) erteilt worden ist und die in das Berufsregister der zuständigen Steuerberaterkammer eingetragen sind." It adds: "Die Befugnis zur Hilfeleistung in Steuersachen der in dem Verzeichnis gelisteten Personen umfasst nur die Tätigkeiten, für die partieller Zugang gewährt wurde." FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: A permission for partial access granted under § 3d(1) StBerG together with entry in the professional register of the competent regional Steuerberaterkammer; published federally under § 3g StBerG. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundessteuerberaterkammer, a public-law professional chamber. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: A berufs-org.de subdomain of its own, separate from the chamber’s two other statutory registers. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public search at partiell-zugelassene-personen-in-steuersachen.berufs-org.de. Separation decision: distinct statutory basis (§ 3g), a materially different entitlement and its own host, separate from both the § 86b main register and the § 3b temporary-provider register.

name: Verzeichnis der gemeldeten Unternehmen
description: The German directory of undertakings that have notified the Federal Network Agency under section 5 of the Telecommunications Act. It is a statutory publication rather than a searchable register: the agency publishes it periodically as a spreadsheet giving each undertaking’s name, address and a short description of the notified activity.

publicAccess.notes: The agency’s page was served anonymously with no credential and links the directory as a downloadable spreadsheet dated 5 August 2026, so login is recorded as not required. The spreadsheet was not downloaded or opened, so its contents, completeness and any limits were not observed and stay null. There is no search interface to exercise.

bestFor: Obtaining the full German list of notified telecommunications undertakings as a single dataset.
Establishing the statutory notification duty that sits behind German telecoms market entry.
notRecommendedFor: Looking up one company quickly. There is no search interface; the directory is published as a periodic spreadsheet.
Checking an email or messaging service. Number-independent interpersonal telecommunications services are expressly exempt from the notification duty.
pros: Its statutory basis is quoted by the agency itself: section 5 of the Telecommunications Act creates the notification duty, and section 5(4) requires the agency to publish this directory regularly.
The published directory carries a dated snapshot, so a reader knows exactly what point in time the list represents.
The agency states what the directory contains — names, addresses and a short description of the notified activity — so its scope is not left to inference.
cons: Entry follows a NOTIFICATION, not a licence. Section 5 requires an undertaking to notify intended commencement, change and termination of activity; the agency grants nothing.
It is published as a periodic spreadsheet download rather than a live searchable register, so a reader gets a dated snapshot and must re-download to see changes.

Number-independent interpersonal telecommunications services such as email and messenger services are expressly exempt from the notification duty, so absence does not establish that a service is unregulated — other duties may still apply to them.

Being recorded here proves nothing about spectrum or numbering. Notification as an operator, an individual spectrum authorisation and an allocation of numbers are three separate legal acts kept in three separate systems. German spectrum and numbering are administered separately by the same agency.
The spreadsheet was not opened during verification, so nothing about its contents, field coverage or completeness is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the agency’s own telecommunications obligations section, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The agency states "§ 5 Telekommunikationsgesetz (TKG) ist die gesetzliche Grundlage der Meldepflicht" and quotes the provision, including that it does not apply to "nummernunabhängige interpersonelle Telekommunikationsdienste". It further states: "Gemäß § 5 Abs. 4 TKG veröffentlicht die Bundesnetzagentur regelmäßig ein Verzeichnis der gemeldeten Unternehmen. Dieses Verzeichnis enthält die Namen und Anschriften der anbietenden Unternehmen sowie eine Kurzbeschreibung der gemeldeten Tätigkeit." The directory was published as "Gemeldete Unternehmen (Stand 05.08.2026) (xlsx / 301 KB)". The agency also states it transmits section 5(2) data to BEREC for the Union database under § 5 Abs. 6 TKG, which is how the BEREC GADB record was reached. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The notification made by the undertaking under § 5 TKG. The agency records and publishes it under § 5 Abs. 4 TKG; nothing is granted. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundesnetzagentur. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The directory is published as a spreadsheet on the agency’s own bundesnetzagentur.de domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The Meldepflicht page, which is where the agency publishes both the notification form and the directory. There is no separate search application, so the page is recorded as the public access interface. Publication-form decision: this download IS the register’s official published form under § 5 Abs. 4 TKG, which is why it is published here — unlike the German audit chamber’s Article 16(3) list rejected in Wave 3A-2, which was a publication DERIVED from a register that also had its own searchable interface.

name: Anbieterverzeichnis für Postdienstleistungen
description: The German directory of postal service providers, kept by the Federal Network Agency. Entry is constitutive rather than declaratory: since 18 July 2024 postal services may be provided only by entered providers, and a provider may subcontract only to another entered provider. It is a different legal act from the agency’s telecommunications notification directory, which it sits alongside.

publicAccess.notes: Result rows were rendered to an anonymous client with no credential and no payment, showing registration number, company, postcode, town, address, country and entry date. Free public reading is therefore observed rather than inferred. The record count, the "Stand" date and the hit counter are filled by JavaScript and showed placeholders to a non-executing client, so no total, currency date or coverage figure was observed and none is asserted. No filtered query was submitted, so behaviour under a specific search and any rate limit stay null.

bestFor: Checking whether a company may lawfully provide postal services in Germany.
Checking a subcontractor before instructing it, because a provider may only commission an entered provider.
notRecommendedFor: Checking a telecommunications undertaking. Postal entry and the agency’s telecommunications notification are different legal acts in different directories.
Assuming entry proves universal-service status or any particular service quality. It records entitlement to provide postal services and nothing more.
pros: Entry is constitutive, not declaratory: the agency states that postal services may only be provided by providers entered in the directory, which makes a search here legally meaningful rather than merely informative.
It reaches the supply chain: a provider may commission another provider only if that provider is entered, so the directory is the correct check before subcontracting.
Rows are readable without an account or payment, and each carries an entry date so a reader can see how long a provider has been entered.
It records whether a provider offers formal service of documents, which is a legally significant capability rather than a marketing claim.
cons: This is entry on application, not a notification and not a licence in the telecommunications sense. A provider must apply and be entered before starting activity; the agency does not merely record a declaration.

A transitional regime was still running at verification. Providers notified under the former section 36 of the Postal Act before 18 July 2024 may continue only until 18 August 2026, and only if they applied by 20 July 2026 — after which continuing to provide postal services is unlawful. During that window the directory does not yet show every lawful provider.

It is a POSTAL directory kept by the same agency that keeps the telecommunications notification directory. Entry here says nothing about whether a company is a telecommunications undertaking, holds spectrum, or holds numbers.
Entry records entitlement. It is not a statement about delivery quality, reliability, solvency, or whether any particular item was handled properly.

Absence does not by itself establish that a company may not deliver anything. During the transitional window a former section 36 notifier may still be operating lawfully, and services outside the statutory definition of postal services are not covered here.
The directory’s own record count and currency date are rendered by JavaScript and were not observed, so no total and no "as at" date is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the agency’s postal section, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass in which all five quotations below matched contiguous official text and the register still rendered rows. The agency states: "Die Bundesnetzagentur führt ein öffentlich einsehbares digitales Verzeichnis aller Anbieter von Postdienstleistungen." and "Postdienstleistungen dürfen nur noch von Anbietern erbracht werden, die in das sogenannte "Anbieterverzeichnis" eingetragen sind." It adds: "Anbieter dürfen einen anderen Anbieter nur dann mit der Erbringung von Postdienstleistungen beauftragen, wenn dieser in das Anbieterverzeichnis eingetragen ist."; that a provider not covered by the transitional rule "muss vor Aufnahme der Tätigkeit bei der Bundesnetzagentur die Aufnahme in das Anbieterverzeichnis beantragen"; that pre-18-July-2024 notifiers "können ihre Tätigkeit noch bis zum 18. August 2026 fortsetzen"; and that without a timely application "ist die weitere Erbringung von Postdienstleistungen unzulässig". The register renders columns Stammnr., Firma, PLZ, Ort, Anschrift, Land, Förm. Zustell. and Eintragung. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Entry in the Anbieterverzeichnis under the German Postal Act as amended from 18 July 2024. Entry follows an application and is a precondition of providing postal services. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Bundesnetzagentur. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: The agency’s own bundesnetzagentur.de host, which also serves its telecommunications notification directory as a separate system. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public directory page at bundesnetzagentur.de. SHARED-HOST DECISION: this record and de-bnetza-verzeichnis-gemeldeter-unternehmen sit on one host and are two materially different statutory systems — postal entry on application versus telecommunications notification under § 5 TKG — covering different populations under different Acts. Both declare resourceIdentity in the bundesnetzagentur-de group with distinct systemKeys. They are neither merged nor treated as views of each other. POSTAL SCOPE DECISION: postal is published as its own record rather than folded under telecommunications, even though one agency supervises both, in line with the wave contract. The record uses the postal population and states explicitly that entry says nothing about telecommunications status.

name: Gelbe Seiten
description: The German Yellow Pages business directory. A basic entry is free and is submitted through the platform’s own entry service, after which it is passed to the regionally responsible Gelbe Seiten publisher for editorial review — so an entry is requested rather than published directly.
bestFor: German local businesses wanting a free listing in a long-established national directory.
Building a German local citation with a named regional publisher behind it.
notRecommendedFor: Anyone needing an entry to appear immediately. Every submission goes to a regional publisher for editorial review first.
Businesses outside Germany. The entry service is organised around German regional publishers.
reviewProcess: Submitted data is sent to the regionally responsible Gelbe Seiten publisher, where it undergoes editorial review before appearing.
pros: A basic entry is free and the operator says so plainly: “Ein kostenloser Grundeintrag bei Gelbe Seiten beinhaltet grundlegende Firmendaten wie die Firmenadresse, Telefonnummer und Öffnungszeiten.”
Submissions are editorially reviewed rather than published automatically, which is unusual among free directories and works against spam.
The regionally responsible publisher is named as the party that receives and checks the data, so there is an accountable human process behind an entry.
Corrections to an existing entry can be requested from within the entry itself.
cons: An entry is a REQUEST, not a publication. The operator states that submitted data “werden an den für Ihre Region zuständigen Gelbe Seiten Verlag geschickt. Dort erfolgt eine redaktionelle Prüfung.”

Creating an entry is confirmed; taking control of an existing third-party entry is not. Changes to an existing entry are requested through the publisher, which is a correction route rather than an established claim of ownership, so no claim flow is asserted here.
The operator does not document whether verification is required or by what method, so nothing about verification is asserted.
The operator does not document a review system or owner responses on the pages consulted, so neither is asserted. Absence here means unrecorded, not unavailable.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, or has been checked beyond the publisher’s editorial review of the submitted data.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own entry service at gelbeseiten.de/starteintrag, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “Grundeintrag”, “kostenloser Grundeintrag bei Gelbe Seiten”, “redaktionelle Prüfung” and “zuständigen Gelbe Seiten Verlag” were each present in the served page. PLATFORM OPERATOR: Gelbe Seiten Verlage, identified on the site as “Ein Service Ihrer Gelbe Seiten Verlage”. LISTING CONTROL: The business submits an entry; the regionally responsible publisher decides whether it appears. Control is therefore shared, not self-service. MODERATION AUTHORITY: The regional Gelbe Seiten publisher, through a stated editorial review (“redaktionelle Prüfung”). PUBLIC INTERFACE: gelbeseiten.de, with the entry service at /starteintrag. DUPLICATE DECISION: kept separate from Das Telefonbuch and 11880. The three reference one another as partner services and share a market, but each operates its OWN entry service on its OWN domain with its OWN editorial process — Gelbe Seiten routes to regional Gelbe Seiten publishers specifically. CORRECTED 2026-08-06: an earlier version of this note said that no operator claims one submission produces entries in the others. That was wrong. DTM Deutsche Tele Medien’s entry service states “Mit nur 1 Klick direkt in 3 Verzeichnissen” and names Das Telefonbuch, Gelbe Seiten and Das Örtliche. A combined submission route therefore DOES exist. The records stay separate because each directory is its own product on its own domain with its own publisher and its own independent entry service; what is shared is one optional combined form, not a listing identity. Shared ownership or cross-linking is not evidence of one system. NOT ASSERTED: verification, reviews, owner responses, indexability, link attributes, traffic. None was documented by the operator and none is inferred.

name: Das Telefonbuch
description: The German national telephone and business directory. A basic business entry is free and is created through the platform’s own Firmeneintrag service, which is separate from the entry services of the other German directories it links to.
bestFor: German businesses wanting a free entry in the country’s long-established telephone directory.
Adding a German local citation alongside, rather than instead of, the other national directories.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses expecting one submission to populate Gelbe Seiten or Das Örtliche. Nothing on the service states that it does.
Anyone relying on documented verification. The operator publishes none.
pros: The basic business entry is explicitly free — the service is described as “Ihr kostenloser Firmeneintrag in Das Telefonbuch”.
The entry service is a plain, dedicated route at a stable address rather than a sales funnel.
The published entry supports substantive business data including web address, telephone, category and opening hours.
cons: Creating an entry is confirmed; claiming an existing one is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.
The operator does not state whether verification is required or by what method. Nothing about verification is asserted.
No review system or owner response capability is documented on the pages consulted, so neither is asserted.
The site links to Gelbe Seiten and Das Örtliche as separate services, and no operator states that one entry reaches all three. A business wanting presence in each must submit to each.
The operator is identified on the site only as joint publishers rather than a single named company, so the corporate entity behind the directory is not established here.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own Firmeneintrag service, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “kostenlos” and “Firmeneintrag” were both present in the served page. The homepage identifies the publisher only as “Gemeinsame Herausgeber und Verleger”, so the operator is recorded under the directory’s own name rather than a company that was not established. PLATFORM OPERATOR: Das Telefonbuch, published by joint publishers named collectively on the site rather than as a single company. LISTING CONTROL: The business creates its own entry through the Firmeneintrag service. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented by the operator. PUBLIC INTERFACE: dastelefonbuch.de, with the entry service at /Firmeneintrag. DUPLICATE DECISION: kept separate from Gelbe Seiten and 11880. Its entry service is its own, on its own domain, and the footer treats the other directories as separate linked services. CORRECTED 2026-08-06: this record previously said its entry page carries no statement that a submission reaches another directory. That remains true of dastelefonbuch.de itself, but it was being used to imply no such route exists anywhere, and one does: DTM Deutsche Tele Medien’s entry service publishes to Das Telefonbuch, Gelbe Seiten and Das Örtliche from a single form. The records stay separate on product and publisher grounds, not on the absence of a combined route. NOT ASSERTED: verification, reviews, owner responses, moderation, indexability, link attributes, traffic.

name: 11880.com
description: A German business directory operated by 11880 Solutions AG, successor to the former telephone directory enquiry company. A basic company entry is free, and company profiles carry customer ratings.
bestFor: German local businesses wanting a free entry on a directory whose profiles carry customer ratings.
Adding a German citation on a platform with a named, identifiable operating company.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses assuming they can reply to ratings. Owner responses are not documented and are not asserted here.
Anyone treating the operator’s paid review-management product as evidence of what the free entry includes.
pros: A basic entry is free and stated as such — the site offers “Gratis: Ihre Firma eintragen”.
The operating company is named and traceable: 11880 Solutions AG, successor to telegate AG and klicktel AG.
Company profiles carry customer ratings, so the directory supports reputation as well as discovery.
A dedicated business section exists for owners rather than only a consumer-facing search.
cons: Ratings exist, but whether a business owner can respond to them is NOT documented, so no owner-response capability is asserted.
The operator sells a paid review-management product. That is a separate commercial offering and is not evidence that responding to ratings is included in the free entry.
Creating an entry is confirmed; claiming an existing profile is not documented, so no claim flow is asserted.
Whether verification is required, and by what method, is not documented.
A rating on a profile reflects what reviewers submitted. It is not a check of whether the business is solvent, licensed or currently trading.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “Ihre Firma eintragen”, “Gratis”, “Bewertungen”, “11880 Solutions” and “kostenlos” were each present in the served page. The first re-verification attempt timed out and the second succeeded; the failure was transport, not content. PLATFORM OPERATOR: 11880 Solutions AG, described on the site as the successor to telegate AG and klicktel AG. LISTING CONTROL: The business creates its own entry through the free registration route. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented by the operator. PUBLIC INTERFACE: 11880.com, with a separate business section for owners. EVIDENCE CAUTION: an automated page summariser initially reported that owner responses are supported, citing the presence of a paid “Bewertungsmanagement” product. That is a commercial offering, not documentation of the free entry, and the inference was rejected. ownerResponseSupport stays null. DUPLICATE DECISION: kept separate from Gelbe Seiten and Das Telefonbuch — different operating company, different entry route, different domain. NOT ASSERTED: verification, owner responses, moderation, indexability, link attributes, traffic.

name: wlw (Wer liefert was)
description: A German-language B2B supplier marketplace covering the DACH region. Suppliers create a company profile and upload product data to be found by professional buyers, which makes it a procurement discovery platform rather than a local business directory.
bestFor: German-speaking B2B suppliers wanting to be found by professional buyers in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
Manufacturers and wholesalers whose discovery problem is procurement rather than local footfall.
notRecommendedFor: Local consumer-facing businesses. This is a B2B procurement marketplace, not a local directory.
Anyone assuming a basic profile is free. The cost of a basic profile is NOT documented and is recorded as unknown.
pros: The population is stated plainly: the platform describes itself as covering “600.000 B2B-Anbieter” and as “der meistbesuchte B2B-Marktplatz für den professionellen Einkauf in der DACH-Region”.
Profiles carry product data, not just contact details, which is what a procurement search actually needs.
Its reach is regional rather than national — Germany, Austria and Switzerland — which suits suppliers who already sell across DACH.
cons: Whether a basic profile is free is NOT documented. A premium profile is offered on request, but the existence of a paid tier does not establish that the basic tier is free, so cost is recorded as unknown.
It is a B2B marketplace. Presence here says nothing about local or consumer visibility, and it is the wrong platform for a business whose customers are the public.
Supplier badges indicate that some verification exists, but the operator does not document what is required or how it is checked, so nothing about verification is asserted.
No review system is documented, so neither reviews nor owner responses are asserted.

Coverage is described as the DACH region rather than Germany alone, so a record filed under Germany understates its geography. The dataset does not yet carry a machine-readable coverage field, and this is stated in prose instead.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “B2B” and “Firmenprofil” were both present in the served page. Profile creation is confirmed by “Erstellen Sie ein Firmenprofil und laden Sie Ihre Produktdaten hoch, um neue Käufer zu gewinnen”, with a supplier registration route at /de/supplier-registration. PLATFORM OPERATOR: wlw (Wer liefert was), a B2B marketplace operator. LISTING CONTROL: The supplier creates and maintains its own company profile and product data. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented by the operator. PUBLIC INTERFACE: wlw.de, with supplier registration on the same domain. COST DECISION: an automated summariser characterised the basic profile as “appears available”, which is not evidence. submissionModel is recorded as unknown rather than free. The brief forbids inferring free from the presence of a registration route, and forbids inferring paid from the presence of a premium tier. name: Das Örtliche
description: One of Germany’s three long-established telephone and business directories. Its entry service is run by DTM Deutsche Tele Medien and is notable for what it does openly: a single free submission places a business in Das Örtliche, Das Telefonbuch and Gelbe Seiten at once.
bestFor: German businesses wanting one free submission that reaches three established national directories.
Businesses that would otherwise submit separately to Das Telefonbuch and Gelbe Seiten.
notRecommendedFor: Businesses that want to appear in exactly one directory. This route deliberately publishes to three.
Businesses outside Germany. The service is organised around German directory publishers.
pros: The entry is free and the operator states it without qualification: “Ihr Eintrag. Mit nur 1 Klick direkt in 3 Verzeichnissen. Kostenfrei.”
One submission reaches three of Germany’s best-known directories: “Freuen Sie sich auf Ihren Eintrag in Das Telefonbuch, Gelbe Seiten und Das Örtliche.”
The operator is named plainly as DTM Deutsche Tele Medien GmbH, with separate documented routes for creating, editing and deleting an entry.
Both new entries and changes to an existing one are handled through the same service: “Hier können Sie sich oder Ihre Firma neu eintragen oder Ihren bestehenden Eintrag verwalten.”
cons: A submission is not confined to this directory. The same form publishes to Das Telefonbuch and Gelbe Seiten, which is convenient but removes the choice of appearing in only one.
The directory itself is a separate surface from the entry service: dasoertliche.de carries the listings, dtme.de takes the submissions. A business must leave the directory to manage its own data.
Creating and updating an entry are documented; taking control of an existing third-party entry as its owner is not described as a claim process, so no claim flow is asserted.
Whether verification is required, and by what method, is not documented, so nothing about verification is asserted.
No review system or owner-response function is documented on the pages consulted, so neither is asserted. Absence here means unrecorded, not unavailable.
No Domain Rating is published for this platform. No valid measurement exists in the frozen historical set and none may be estimated, so the metric is recorded as not measured rather than guessed.
A listing is a directory entry. It is not evidence that a business is solvent, currently trading, licensed, or checked beyond what the operator documents here.
No ranking, indexing, traffic or lead outcome is asserted. The operator markets outcomes; this record does not adopt them.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 from the operator’s own entry service at dtme.de and the directory at dasoertliche.de, and re-verified in a separate direct pass in which “Mit nur 1 Klick direkt in 3 Verzeichnissen”, “Kostenfrei”, “Freuen Sie sich auf Ihren Eintrag in Das Telefonbuch, Gelbe Seiten und Das Örtliche” and “DTM Deutsche Tele Medien GmbH” were each present in the served pages. PLATFORM OPERATOR: DTM Deutsche Tele Medien GmbH, named on its own entry-service site, which the directory links to as its submission route. LISTING CONTROL: The business submits through DTM and can update or delete its entry through the same service. MODERATION AUTHORITY: Not documented. PUBLIC INTERFACE: dasoertliche.de for the directory, dtme.de/ihr-eintrag for submissions. DUPLICATE DECISION: published as its own record despite the shared entry service. The three German directories remain separate PRODUCTS on separate domains with separate publishers and separate public surfaces; what they share is one optional combined submission route. A shared submission form is not the same as a shared listing identity, and a reader choosing where to appear still faces three distinct directories. CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER WAVE: the Gelbe Seiten and Das Telefonbuch records previously stated that no operator claims one submission produces entries in the others. DTM states exactly that. Both records have been corrected in this wave. DOMAIN RATING: null. dasoertliche.de carries no historical measurement and no value may be estimated. NOT ASSERTED: verification, reviews, owner responses, claim flow, indexability, link attributes, traffic.
